hypotheses.claim: ClayCode reference tokens should be delimiter-aware or contextually parsed so structural delimiters cannot become part of an unescaped Ref identity.
support: EXP-CC-LEXICAL-CLOSURE-20260809-01: current matcher overconsumed 10000/10000 adjacent-ref cases
candidate delimiter-aware matcher failed 0/10000 matched cases
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: The production parser already uses contextual delimiter termination and the broad EBNF prose is harmless documentation shorthand.
hypotheses.falsifier: Admitted canonical parser accepts and roundtrips all current delimiter-adjacent refs without a grammar or lexer delta.

hypotheses.claim: Separating bare identifiers from explicit escaped/sigil/quoted symbol identifiers is likely to reduce operator ambiguity while preserving compatibility better than globally forbidding hyphens.
support: current bare-id/minus family collided in 10000/10000 generated unspaced cases
simple hyphen removal resolved the tested ambiguity but also rejected all tested hyphenated names
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: A contextual/precedence-aware lexer can retain hyphenated bare identifiers and minus without materially harming deterministic roundtrip or compiler complexity.
hypotheses.falsifier: Repository-wide corpus plus parser differential shows the current identifier class is deterministic, low-repair-cost and roundtrip-stable across no-space arithmetic and admitted hyphenated symbols.

hypotheses.claim: Lexer/parser policy and grammar/compiler version belong in provenance/contract identity, while ProgramSemanticId should be computed from canonical typed IR after successful parsing rather than raw source token spelling.
support: concurrent ClayCode evidence already separates static program semantic identity from execution/replay identity
this run shows lexical policy can change source interpretation before canonical IR exists
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Raw source hashing is sufficient for all identity roles and a separate post-parse semantic identity adds no correctness value.
hypotheses.falsifier: A matched source-equivalence corpus shows raw-source identity gives equal deduplication, roundtrip, migration and replay correctness without false distinctions or collisions.
